How to Submit an Event or Request a New Calendar

If you are part of NYU Grossman School of Medicine and would like to submit an event, choose a specific calendar and click the “Submit an Event” button, and then log in with your Kerberos ID and password to complete the event submission form. Your request will be reviewed by the calendar’s manager.

To request a new calendar, please fill out a public website content request form. For the Request Type field, select med.nyu.edu and then provide the details about your new calendar request. Please also use this content request form if you already have a calendar and would like to have your events pull into your med.nyu.edu site.

For general information, browse our frequently asked questions. (Kerberos ID and password required).

events.name: Bach Sonatas and Partitas for Solo Violin
events.description:
<p>Grammy Award-winning violinist Jennifer Koh&mdash;&quot;a masterly Bach interpreter&quot;&nbsp;<em>(The New York Times)</em>&mdash;returns with a rare and ambitious undertaking: performing J.S. Bach&#39;s complete Sonatas and Partitas for Solo Violin in a single program. This landmark performance offers a complete journey through one of the violin repertoire&rsquo;s defining masterpieces.</p>
<p>Please note the earlier start time. This program will last approximately 3 hours, with one 30-minute intermission.</p>

events.name: Book Launch: Nita Noveno
events.description: Please join us for a reading with Nita Noveno (Nonfiction, 2002 ) as she sits down with Gina Apostol to discuss her memoir Mud on the Moon.About the Book:Mud on the Moon is a hybrid memoir that intertwines a daughter’s exploration of her Filipino immigrant father’s obscured past with a reimagined version of his untold story. Born in Southeast Alaska, Nita Noveno traces the legacy of her father, who arrived in the US in 1928 as part of a wave of Filipino men seeking better opportunities through manual labor in agriculture and other industries. The book alternates between Nita’s coming-of-age story and imagined chapters of her father’s life, revealing the gaps and silences that lie between their experiences. With a blend of personal and historical imagery, Mud on the Moon offers a rare glimpse into the lives of Filipino immigrants in America. It is a meditation on how family, memory, and identity are shaped by the stories we inherit, both spoken and unspoken, across generations.“Mud on the Moon is a lyrical, innovative memoir linking Philippine history to the American present, and the American past to Filipino lives, asking us to see contemporary America, especially but not only Filipino America, in novel ways, in both meanings of that word: as a complex and layered narrative demanding to be told and as an art experiment raising stakes on not only what it means to be American but also what it means to make art. Risk-taking, clear-eyed, but always artful, engaging, and above all embracing of multiple worlds and times, Noveno is a voice for our complex moment.”—Gina Apostol, author of La Tercera and Insurrecto“Mud on the Moon is a beautiful story of a daughter in the act of knowing her father. Noveno collects and creates the threads of his story, stitching and restitching memories, records, artifacts, history, mystery, and fiction. A delight of formal invention, this memoir brilliantly weaves narrative and photograph, father and daughter, fact and fiction, creating a moving, rich, multifaceted portrayal of the life of her father, a Filipino immigrant to the US, and her own.”—Ananda Lima, author of Craft: Stories I Wrote for the Devil and Mother/land

events.name: In Conversation with Ilaria Resta, CEO of Audemars Piguet
events.description: We are pleased to welcome Ilaria Resta, Chief Executive Officer of Audemars Piguet, to speak with our students. With nearly three decades of global leadership experience across some of the world's most respected luxury brands, Ilaria has built a career defined by innovation, purpose-driven leadership, and a commitment to empowering people. Since becoming CEO of Audemars Piguet, she has led the Manufacture with a vision that honors its rich heritage while shaping its future through creativity, craftsmanship, and sustainable growth. Guided by the principles of Love, Learn, and Legacy, Ilaria believes leadership is about serving others, fostering curiosity, and creating lasting impact. During her conversation with our students, she will share insights from her leadership journey, discuss the evolving landscape of the luxury industry, and reflect on what it takes to build meaningful careers rooted in purpose, innovation, and excellence.

events.name: Darkology: Blackface and the American Way of Entertainment
events.description: ﻿The Center for the American Experience invites you to join Rhae Lynn Barnes, Assistant Professor of History at Princeton University, and Jonathan Square, Assistant Professor of Black Visual Culture at Parsons, for a discussion of Barnes's book Darkology: Blackface and the American Way of Entertainment. Darkology is a major study of the history of blackface minstrelsy in the United States, showing how deeply it shaped American entertainment, institutions, and racial politics from the nineteenth century through the Civil Rights era and beyond. Drawing on extensive archival research, Barnes challenges the idea that blackface was marginal or short-lived, revealing instead how widely it spread across schools, churches, universities, military spaces, and public life.

events.name: Book Launch: Molly McCloy
events.description: Please join us for a reading with Molly McCloy (Nonfiction, 2006) as she sits down with Luis Jaramillo, Associate Professor of Writing and Chair of Fiction, to discuss her memoir Nine Grudges: The Spiteful Origins of the Happiest Dyke on Earth.About the Book:"On the cusp of her 1993 college graduation in Olympia, Molly McCloy spends her time drunk and high, pulling dykey pranks, and thrashing in mosh pits—anything to avoid the troubled, working-class family she left behind in Arizona. But after a vivid nightmare involving her dad, Molly writes him a letter, asking him to apologize for nine instances of mental, verbal, and physical abuse. She revisits each of these nine grudges before working up enough courage to mail the letter. Then, to her surprise, her dad writes back. "Nine Grudges grabs hold of you like a best friend ready to divulge terrible, wonderful secrets. Funny, soulful, absolutely unafraid to look life in the eye, Molly McCloy’s tough and tender voice is addictive. An electric debut!"—Michelle Tea, author of Knocking Myself Up "Nine Grudges shouldn’t be funny, but it is simultaneously hilarious and chilling. Like Dorothy Allison in Bastard Out of Carolina, McCloy has a powerful voice, a poet’s ear, and amazing recall".—Ann Cummins, Red Ant House and Yellowcake

events.name: Welcome to The Center for the American Experience: Launch Celebration
events.description: The Center for the American Experience (CAE) at The New School invites you to a special evening featuring biographer and public servant Walter Isaacson in conversation with CAE Co-Director and historian Natalia Mehlman Petrzela on the theme of “American Stories,” the narratives about individuals, ideals, and experiences through which a nation comes to understand itself. The Mannes Orchestra, led by maestro David Hayes, will perform Charles Ives’s Variations on “America,” a work that takes a shared national symbol and reinvents it, playfully, in several keys at once.We will also mark the launch of CAE—a nonpartisan home for bold scholarly, creative, and civic engagement with the nation’s past, present, and place in the world. At a moment of deep polarization, CAE is dedicated to fostering pluralism, dialogue, and fearless debate.Join us in celebrating the many voices, sounds, and stories that shape the American experience.

events.name: John Lewis: A Life
events.description: The Center for the American Experience invites you to join David Greenberg, Professor of Journalism and Media Studies at Rutgers University, and Claire Bond Potter, Emerita Professor of Historical Studies at The New School, for a discussion of Greenberg’s new book, John Lewis: A Life. The book is a sweeping and analytically nuanced biography of one of the most enduring figures of the civil rights movement, situating Lewis as both a moral and political actor whose life reshaped the trajectory of American democracy. Drawing on extensive archival research and newly available sources, Greenberg traces Lewis’s journey from his youth in rural Alabama and early encounters with racial violence to his leadership in nonviolent protest and his decades in Congress. Attentive to the ethical discipline of nonviolence as well as the internal tensions of movement politics, the book offers a richly layered account of political commitment, illuminating the vision, courage, and persistence that defined Lewis’s lifelong struggle for justice. Described as “an authoritative and compelling portrait of a defining figure in American public life” by The New York Times, the book underscores the enduring relevance of Lewis’s legacy.

It's your choice, we want as many people as possible to enjoy the music.Those who register for the livestream will receive a viewing link 24 hours before the concert.The link will become active about 15 minutes before the live concert begins.This concert is part of the Schneider Concerts 2026-2027 season: In 6 mainstage concerts featuring exceptional emerging ensembles, livestreams, pre-concert talks, and free short programs at community partner venues we explore the place we carry. Composers and chamber musicians bring nature into cities, transform urban rhythms into music, and weave memories, family histories, and migration stories into their work, reflecting and engaging cultural identity as vital members of their communities. Explore the entire 2026-2027 season here.If you have questions, please contact us at nsc@newschool.edu or (212) 229-5873
